title: I posted a comment and it vanished
summary: Reads from a lagging replica show a user the page before their own comment; read-your-writes sends their reads to the primary until the replica catches up.

takeaway.summary: Keep the version of the session's last confirmed write, and let the replica serve a read only once it has applied that version; otherwise read from the primary.
whenToUse: Reads go to replicas, and users expect to see what they just wrote: comments, profile edits, settings
Any copy that can lag behind the store that confirms writes

scenes.narration: Ana posts a comment and sees posted. She reloads the page and her comment isn't there, then it comes back a few seconds later. Writes go to a primary database; reads go to a replica, a copy that spreads the load.
scenes.caption: Ana posts a comment, reloads, and it's gone. A moment later it's back

scenes.narration: Ana's comment becomes version 51 on the primary, which confirms it at 3507 milliseconds. A lag spike started at 3 seconds, so the replication stream is still carrying version 51 to the replica, which has applied up to version 49.
scenes.caption: The primary confirms v51, but the replica has applied only up to v49

scenes.narration: Ana reloads 300 milliseconds later. The app reads from the replica, which is still at version 49, so the page comes back without her comment. Nothing was lost: the replica just hasn't caught up.
scenes.caption: Ana reloads: the replica returns v49, so her comment seems to vanish

scenes.narration: She reloads a second later: still version 49. At 5347 milliseconds the replica applies version 51, 1.8 seconds after the primary committed it, and Ana's next reload shows her comment again, which is even more confusing.
scenes.caption: The replica applies v51 after 1.8 s, and Ana's comment is back

scenes.narration: How often does this happen? Rerun the same traffic, spike included, at four mean lags: of 18 reloads right after a post, 9 came back without the comment at 50 milliseconds, 11 at 200, 17 at 500, and all 18 at 1000.
scenes.caption: Stale reloads right after a write: 9, 11, 17, 18 of 18 as mean lag grows

scenes.narration: The fix is read-your-writes. The session keeps a token, the version of its last confirmed write. The replica serves a read only if it has applied at least that version; otherwise the read goes to the primary.
scenes.caption: Remember your last write's version; read the replica only once it has it

elements.reason: the primary always has every confirmed write
elements.label: where to read

scenes.narration: Replay the same moment with the fix. Ana's reload carries her token, version 51. The replica has applied only version 49, so the app sends the read to the primary, and her comment is there.
scenes.caption: Same spike: Ana's token is v51, the replica has v49, so she reads the primary

scenes.narration: Rerun the four lags with read-your-writes: none of the 18 reloads right after a post comes back without the comment, at any lag.
scenes.caption: With the fix: 0 of 18 stale reloads at every mean lag

scenes.narration: The fix isn't free. The primary, which otherwise takes about 2 writes a second, now serves 3.7 reads a second at 50 milliseconds of lag and 6.4 at 1000, up to 20 percent of all reads. The more the replica lags, the more load moves back.
scenes.caption: The cost: 3.7 to 6.4 reads a second move to the primary as lag grows

scenes.narration: Checked over seeds 1 to 20, mean lags of 50, 200, 500, and 1000 milliseconds, with and without the spike, and reloads 100, 300, and 1000 milliseconds after posting: reading the replica broke the rule in 469 of 480 runs, read-your-writes in none. It needs one primary taking every write in order, the token on every read of the session, and no failover to a replica missing a confirmed write.
scenes.caption: Checked over 480 runs: no fix 469 broken, read-your-writes 0

elements.title: Runs where a user saw the past
elements.detail: Seeds 1–20 × 4 lags × spike on/off × 3 reload delays
